import FormalConjecturesUtil
import FormalConjectures.OEIS.«3625»

/-!
# $a(n) = \sum_{k=0}^n \binom{2k}{k}^3$

The sequence $a(n) = 1 + \binom{2}{1}^3 + \binom{4}{2}^3 + \cdots + \binom{2n}{n}^3$:
$$a(n) = \sum_{k=0}^n \binom{2k}{k}^3$$

*References:*
- [A079727](https://oeis.org/A079727)-/

namespace OeisA79727

/-- $a(n) = \sum_{k=0}^n \binom{2k}{k}^3$. -/
def a (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  ∑ k ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), (Nat.choose (2 * k) k) ^ 3

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 0. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_0 : a 0 = 1 := by
  rfl

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 1. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_1 : a 1 = 9 := by
  rfl

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 2. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_2 : a 2 = 225 := by
  rfl

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 3. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_3 : a 3 = 8225 := by
  rfl

/-- Value of the sequence `a` at 4. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_4 : a 4 = 351225 := by
  rfl

/--
Conjecture 1 (Peter Bala, 2024):
If prime $p$ is in A003625 then $a(p^2) \equiv 8 + p^2 \pmod{p^3}$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem conjecture1 (p : ℕ) (hp : OeisA3625.A p) :
    a (p ^ 2) ≡ 8 + p ^ 2 [MOD p ^ 3] := by
  sorry

/--
Conjecture 2 (Peter Bala, 2024):
If prime $p$ is in A003625 then $a(p(p-1)) \equiv p^2 \pmod{p^3}$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem conjecture2 (p : ℕ) (hp : OeisA3625.A p) :
    a (p * (p - 1)) ≡ p ^ 2 [MOD p ^ 3] := by
  sorry

/--
Conjecture 3 (Peter Bala, 2024):
If prime $p$ is in A003625 then $a((p^2-1)/2) \equiv p^2 \pmod{p^4}$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem conjecture3 (p : ℕ) (hp : OeisA3625.A p) :
    a ((p ^ 2 - 1) / 2) ≡ p ^ 2 [MOD p ^ 4] := by
  sorry

/--
Conjecture 4 (Peter Bala, 2024):
If $n$ is a product of distinct primes from A003625 then $a((n-1)/2)$ is divisible by $n^2$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem conjecture4 (S : Finset ℕ) (hS : ∀ p ∈ S, OeisA3625.A p) :
    (∏ p ∈ S, p) ^ 2 ∣ a ((∏ p ∈ S, p - 1) / 2) := by
  sorry

end OeisA79727

reformulations.difference: The source quantifies over numbers n that are products of distinct A003625 primes; Lean quantifies over a finite set S of such primes and also permits S = ∅.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: A Finset records distinct factors without repetition, and substituting n = ∏ p ∈ S, p gives the source's divisibility statement. Conversely, every product of distinct primes has such a finite set of factors. The empty set contributes only n = 1 and the true statement 1 ∣ a 0, so it is harmless even if the source intends a nonempty product. The equivalence with the natural-number formulation requiring a nonempty factorization was proved in /workspace/review/equivalence.lean without using any conjecture axiom.

OEIS A003625, definition and comments: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oeis/oeisdata/main/seq/A003/A003625.seq (official export of https://oeis.org/A003625).

review.notes:
All ten declarations were checked. The sequence definition and five test values agree with OEIS, and all four conjectures faithfully state Bala's comments. Lean checks establish that permitted primes are odd and at least 3, products are positive and odd, and the divisions by 2 are exact. Numerical checks passed for conjectures 1–3 at p = 3, 5, 13, 17, 19 and for several singleton and composite products in conjecture 4.

Importantly, Lean parses `(∏ p ∈ S, p - 1)` as `((∏ p ∈ S, p) - 1)`, not as a product of p−1; this was verified by expansion and an rfl proof. The official OEIS export still records all four as conjectures. Its cited older result proves the prime case a((p−1)/2) ≡ 0 mod p², not the four conjectures in full. Direct OEIS requests were blocked, so the source was read through its current official export. Scratch files compiled successfully, and the reviewed file matches the specified commit exactly.
